## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The timestamp semantics and NULL documentation should be corrected because they give consumers incorrect information about process history.

## Changes
The pull request exposes the latest event’s timestamp as `finished_at` when that event is `started`, adds schema documentation, and adds reviewer-facing text.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — Align finished_at with its documented meaning — For process 20, whose latest event is `started`, you expose its start timestamp as its finish time. The schema defines this column as “Timestamp when the process finished.” — Consumers using a non-null `finished_at` to identify completion will incorrectly classify newly started processes as finished. — Fix: Either compute a completion timestamp or rename and document the column as a start timestamp.
- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — Correct the documented meaning of NULL — For process 30, `started` followed by `cleared` produces NULL despite its recorded start. “NULL means the process has never been started.” contradicts `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end`, which examines only the latest event. — Consumers following this description will mistake previously started, cleared processes for processes that never started.
